established.fact: Official AksharDrishti page publishes NO metric (0 hits for CER/WER/S-D-I/latency/score/weight on rendered 4 tabs + modal). Evaluation = 6 qualitative, unweighted parameters: approach, business use case, technical feasibility, product roadmap, team, addressable market (incl. 4-yr deployment/customization cost).

Only named evaluation target: 'Establishing Standardized Evaluation Pipelines or accuracy, layout detection, and multilingual text handling' - three dimensions, no formula/threshold. Rubric is product/business weighted, not accuracy weighted.

The 'CER+bootstrap CI/WER/S-D-I/sec-per-page' rubric came from a student B.Tech repo (Ayush-04-spec/akshardrishti, K.K. Wagh), not the hackathon; official scoring rules UNKNOWN (U2). Never state it as official.

No official deadline: 10 of 12 timeline rows TBD; only launch 12/02/2026 and pitch screening 23/07/2026 dated. 'Qualifiers 30/09' is the Rajasthan hackathon's; 'Oct 4' and 'Oct 15' have no source (Oct 4 2026 is a Sunday).

Official page promotes open-source models, names baselines Tesseract/EasyOCR/TrOCR/PaddleOCR and architectures LayoutLM/Donut/DocTR; asks layout-preserving JSON + searchable PDF, language detection, transliteration, context-based correction (as a Focus Area, not a stated submission format). '22 languages' appears nowhere on the page.

Official page is a client-rendered SPA; static fetch returns only Timeline. Evaluation/Eligibility/Contact tabs need a rendered browser; Gate-1 licensing cannot close from public pages alone. Organiser contact gic.dibd@gmail.com is a boss outward action.

Bhashini funnel analogues: screening top-5, prototype top-3 (INR 1 Lakh build), deployment contract; LEAP: INR 10L winner + 4-yr govt deployment; judged on innovation, replicability, scalability, usability, ease of deployment, risks. Real prize = deployment contract. AksharDrishti purse unknown.
Eligibility: Indian company or DPIIT startup; employer NOC required; registration can complete at prototype submission. Vinay's side is a registered company (U36 YES).
Writeup must carry a 4-year support/cost sketch, IPR section and deployment+O&M costing; mirror LEAP's six criteria. Demo should lead with governance/archive use case, not a CER table.

No verified AksharDrishti OCR-track winner exists; the Plenome win was healthcare voice-to-prescription (different hackathon). One uncorroborated post says VaultStack AI reached Finals - must confirm stage before any finalist claim.

Bhashini deployment shape: Udyat OCR dhruva-api with serviceIds iiith-bhasha-ocr / iiith-ocr-sceneText-all / iiith-ocr-hw-all; PoC use free, production needs paid tiers. Bhashini throughput cited as 15M vs 24M daily - cite neither.
Winning archetype across 2026 Bhashini hackathons: offline, open-source, native-language, working prototype, citizen service - matches our offline portable harness.

Sarvam Vision 2.1 (2026-09-24): Indic OCR Bench overall 87.39 = unweighted macro word accuracy over 22 Indic languages, n=6,609 (English 300 excluded; total 6,909), per-language n 207-471; self-scored on its own Apache-2.0 bench; exact word_accuracy vs valid_word_accuracy unknown.

Leaderboard on Sarvam's bench (run by Sarvam): Sarvam 87.39, Bodhan 84.94, Gemini 3.6 Flash 79.35, Google Cloud Vision 71.76, Surya OCR 2 69.96, Mistral OCR4 69.16, Opus 5 68.81. Sarvam bench GT reviewed twice by human experts; overlap-with-training is an unverified allegation only.

84.94 is SARVAM's score for Bodhan on Sarvam's bench; Bodhan's own bench number is 86.2 (Sarvam's 86.6 on that bench). 8 of 22 per-language winners flip between the two vendor benches (Kashmiri 54.82/48.04 vs 43.3/52.2). Neither bench is a third-party arbiter.

Sarvam published weak cells: Kashmiri 54.82, Santali 53.91, Odia 80.01. 'OldScan 55.3' is an English olmOCR-Bench category, not a language, and not ours. Konkani 97.41 is Sarvam's BEST cell, not a weak one.

Bodhan IndicOCR is ~0.83B (33M IndicDocLayout + 0.8B IndicBlockOCR Qwen3.5), released 5 Sep 2026, Rs 0.20/image API. Licence is Indic Open Model License v1.0, NOT open source: hosting needs written approval (3.1), internal-component carve-out (3.2), share-alike, 500M MAU/$250M cap; earlier '~3B' and Sep 4/12 dates are wrong.

Bodhan beats Sarvam on Santali on Sarvam's bench (68.30 vs 53.91) and Bodo (90.69 vs 90.48); Bodhan loses 11 of 13 handwriting languages to Gemini 3.1 Pro (72.0 vs 66.7 mean) and 14 of 22 printed languages to Sarvam. Plan v4's Bodhan-HW bn 71.3/Gemini 74.8/Sarvam 58.3 are from the Bodhan card (v4_notes), not in campaign files.

Sarvam 2.1 harness: 3B state-space VLM + semantic layout parser + pointer reading-order net, SFT then RLVR incl. KV-extraction and handwriting corpora; self-admits saturated benchmarks, no decontamination, no per-language CIs. Handwriting is its weakest area on Bodhan's HW bench (Sarvam 55.4 overall).

Nobody publishes handwriting, tables or code-mixed Indic conditions on Indic OCR Bench; handwriting coverage by field benches is only 12 Indic languages. Our own 1,283 printed-benchmark items are 0% table, 0% mixed-script, 100% printed.

On 18 human-verified items Sarvam CER 0.171 vs our best local 0.430 = Sarvam 2.51x better (3.70x vs surya-always; 2.02x excl. mni/sat). All 21 item-level local wins are in the PDF-text-layer GT tier; pooled 'we lead 10/18' is a GT artefact.

Paired Sarvam comparison is only n=54 (3/lang x 18; Sarvam EN cap 57 spent): Sarvam mean CER 0.2640 (0.2400 on probe table), best local 0.2956, surya 0.3944; McNemar p<0.05 in only 5 languages. No further Sarvam calls without explicit boss approval.

Edge hunt on printed 22-language: 4 candidates x 3 adversarial lenses, 0 survived; estimated printed position ~Surya 2 69.96, ~6th of 14, ~17 pts behind Sarvam (ESTIMATE only; superseded for the handwriting test).

Sarvam pricing Rs0.5/page (cut from Rs1.5 in Jun 2026; Rs1.50 also quoted for Vision 2.1), ~Rs2,672 (~$32) for 5,344 pages; Bodhan Rs0.20/image; Mistral OCR 3 $2/1000. Rs100 in the Sep-16 package was free credit, not a price.

Local compute economics: engines on 5,344 images range 0.6 h (rapidocr) to ~36 h (surya 24.3 s/page) to ~25 h (indicphotoocr); paddleocr_indic 95.6 s/page = ~26.5 h per 1000 pages CPU. Best printed engine is slowest by ~60x.

Surya weights: modified OpenRAIL-M, free under ~$5M funding/revenue, s2(c) competing-product and s8 output share-alike clauses; code Apache-2.0. Treat as eval/research only, not a shipped component or label source; CEO decision U14 open.
Test set = Datasets/akshardrishti_official/test/test: 5,344 unlabelled JPGs, 'NEVER train on it'; no language label so script/language ID is needed. Submission format unpublished.

Disqualified/penalised pitch moves: 'agentic AI', unexplained 'combine X and Y', novel backbone; an edge survives only if <2 of 3 adversarial lenses refute it. Honesty law: no fake claims, evidence or silence.

The handwriting edge (planner finding, 2026-10-01): test is Bengali handwritten word crops; IIIT-INDIC-HW-WORDS is CC BY 4.0 (train OK); ICDAR'23 Bengali best WRR 96.10 (Upstage) vs general doc VLMs 58-75 on Bodhan HW bench; HW0 hash check vs IIIT/ICDAR sets must precede any training.

Bodhan D1 (MLX) measured: bench small_rep CER 0.054 / WER 0.1356 (~86.4 word-acc vs published 84.94); 300 gold pairs CER 0.4034 vs surya 0.5660; sample-100 pages CER 0.69 (unexplained); Gate 1 CONDITIONAL PASS only, official-path CUDA parity blocked.
Bodhan model size sources disagree (MLX 4-bit 633 MB vs 767 MB; bf16 1.7 GB vs 1868 MB); 4-bit ~ bf16 on overall metric.

Laya (text-only, near-random on non-Latin: Hindi 0.100) and JEV (closed, paid, 236-276 ms) are ruled NOT used; reopen only if oracle gap >=0.02 CER AND deterministic bad-output check misses >=0.02 recoverable CER.

Printed per-engine CER (probe, 18 langs): surya 0.3849 best non-Sarvam, tesseract-bilingual 0.4853, tess_indic 0.4870, easyocr 0.4941, indicphotoocr 0.5586; surya wins 9 of 13 n>=50 langs; sat/mni have no open engine emitting the script. Directional, GT-tier dependent.

Scorer comparability: our metrics.py counts empties/loops as CER 1.0 and drops GT<50 chars; Sarvam drops loops/empties. A vendor word-accuracy claim and our CER are not comparable without one stated scorer (U16: run Sarvam's public scorer on its Apache-2.0 bench, needs boss approval for download).

Competitor/field intel: Sarvam $75M Series B at $1.43B (2026-08-04); Gnani Evon 3.3 is a text-only LLM, not an OCR competitor; PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 leads OmniDocBench v1.6 (96.01 vs Sarvam 94.97); Chitrapathak-2/Parichay is the govt-doc demo pattern (rotation pre-pass + schema prompt).
